 Agreed Compliance Measures
 (This declaration replaces the one published on May 17, 2023.)
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by public office holders and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist them in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holders and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends. 
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the interests of Université de Montréal or to give preferential treatment to this organization, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself, in my capacity as a public office holder, from any discussion or decision in relation to Université de Montréal. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrators know or reasonably should know to affect the interests of Université de Montreal.
This screen is co-administered by the Executive Vice-President and the Vice-President, Research - Programs of the Canadian Institutes of Health Research (CIHR) to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decisions-making processes involving the interests of Université de Montréal. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect the interests of Université de Montréal as a member of a broad class of organizations unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class. 
The Minister of Health as well as the members of the Governing Council, the Executive Management, the Scientific Directors and staff members of the CIHR have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
